note: What counts as time-sensitive. Used by triage and intake to flag a message for an attorney. Flags never give advice and never state a legal deadline as fact.

categories.label: Court date or hearing
categories.why: A missed hearing can lead to a default ruling.

categories.label: Served with legal papers
categories.why: Papers carry a response deadline that starts when they are served.

categories.label: Filing or response deadline
categories.why: A late response can forfeit rights.

categories.label: Arrest or detention
categories.why: Time matters, and the firm does not handle criminal matters, so a person must point them elsewhere fast.

categories.label: Eviction or lockout
categories.why: A housing deadline can run quickly. The firm does not handle landlord-tenant cases, so a person must point them elsewhere fast.

dateWindowRule: If a message or a notice contains a date of a hearing, response or filing within dayThreshold days of today, flag it as urgent. A date in the past is also flagged, as 'date has passed', because the situation needs a person.
neverDo: State a deadline as a legal fact. Only repeat a date that the sender or the document gave, and mark it 'as written'.
Tell anyone whether they have a case.
Promise that an attorney will act by a given time.
Reply to opposing counsel or the court. Those go to a person.
